;Armed conflicts and attacks
* An explosive device is detonated in a commercial center in the [[Colombia]]n city of [[Cúcuta]], on the border with [[Venezuela]], with at least 12 injured. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20190531/462576819598/detonacion-de-un-explosivo-causa-12-heridos-en-frontera-con-venezuela.html (''La Vanguardia'')] [https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/mundo/al-menos-12-heridos-deja-explosion-en-frontera-entre-colombia-y-venezuela (''El Universal'')]
*Six explosive devices detonated in several locations in [[Kirkuk]], [[Iraq]] kill 5 people and injure 20 others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/at-least-five-dead-in-blasts-in-iraqs-kirkuk-medical-sources-idUSKCN1T02E8 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A suicide bombing near a military training center in the [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] capital city of [[Kabul]] kills 6 people and leaves 6 others injured. The [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province]] claims responsibility [https://www.presstv.com/Detail/2019/05/30/597301/Afghanistan-Kabul-bomb-attack-military-academy (Press TV)]

;Arts and culture
*[[2019 Bilderberg Conference]]
**The annual [[Bilderberg Meeting|meeting]] of the secretive Bilderberg Group takes place at the [[Fairmont Le Montreux Palace]] in [[Montreux]], [[Switzerland]]. The Conference will last for four days. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2019/05/30/pompeo-kushner-head-bilderberg-meeting-mysterious-gathering-global-elite/?utm_term=.69f98b990d8f (''The Washington Post'')]

;Health and environment
*A study, published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', finds a [[Genetic engineering|genetically enhanced]] fungus that produces spider toxin  can rapidly kill huge numbers of the mosquitoes that spread [[malaria]]. Trials held  in [[Burkina Faso]] showed mosquito populations collapsed by 99% within 45 days. The fungus did not affect other insects, such as bees. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-48464510 (BBC News)] [https://science.sciencemag.org/content/364/6443/894 (''Science'')]
*[[Measles resurgence in the United States]]
**Sixty new cases in the past week are reported, bringing this year's total to 971 cases in 26 U.S. states – the highest since 1994. The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] warns, "If these outbreaks continue through summer and fall, the United States may lose its [[Measles#Americas|measles elimination status]]." [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48468801 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Mexico–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces a 5% import tariff on all products from Mexico, effective June 10 and rising in steps to 25% by October, "until the illegal immigration problem is remedied". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48469408 (BBC News)]
**[[President of Mexico|Mexican President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] responds with a letter to the U.S. president stating  he wants to avoid a confrontation, saying that ideals such as justice and universal brotherhood are more important than borders. He  also ordered his [[Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Mexico)|foreign minister]] to travel to Washington on Friday. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-mexico-president/america-first-is-a-fallacy-mexicos-president-responds-to-trump-tariff-idUSKCN1T109N?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*American songwriter [[R. Kelly]] is charged by [[Cook County, Illinois|Cook County]] prosecutors with 11 counts of sexual assault and abuse.  [https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2019/05/30/r-kelly-charged-11-new-counts-sex-abuse/1289868001/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Sinking of Hableány|Sinking of ''Hableány'']]
**The captain of the M/V ''Viking Sigyn'' that was involved in the deadly sinking of the ''Hableány'' is questioned and arrested by the [[Rendőrség|Hungarian police]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48468701 (BBC News)]
*[[Jussie Smollett hate crime hoax]]
**New documents reveal that [[Jussie Smollett]] bought drugs from Abimbola "Abel" and Olabinjo "Ola" Osundairo, the two people who accused him of staging an attack on January 29. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2019/05/31/jussie-smollett-bought-drugs-brothers-who-attacked-him/1296878001/ (''USA Today'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Papua New Guinea]]
**[[James Marape]] is elected [[Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea|Prime Minister]] by the [[National Parliament of Papua New Guinea|National Parliament]] following the resignation of [[Peter O'Neill]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-05-30/papua-new-guinea-announce-new-pm-james-marape/11163006 (ABC)]
*[[Abortion in the United States by state]]
**[[List of governors of Louisiana|Louisiana Governor]] [[John Bel Edwards]] signs a [[heartbeat bill]] that bans abortion as early as six weeks into pregnancy. The law’s effective date is tied to a similar Mississippi law which has already been temporarily blocked by a federal court. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48468962 (BBC News)]
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**Fifteen days after the first wave of protests, millions of students, schoolteachers and university professors hold demonstrations in over a hundred [[Brazil|Brazilian]] cities against massive cuts in the education budget. Brazilian Education Minister Abraham Weintraub accuses teachers of "coercing" students into participating in the protests. [https://amp.theguardian.com/world/2019/may/31/students-protest-across-brazil-over-jair-bolsonaros-sweeping-cuts-to-education (''The Guardian'')]

;Sports
*[[2019 NBA Finals]]
**The [[Toronto Raptors]] host the first [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) [[NBA Finals|finals game]] in their franchise history, against the [[Golden State Warriors]], and the first outside the United States in NBA history at the [[Scotiabank Arena]] in [[Toronto]]. The Raptors win 118–109. [https://www.npr.org/2019/05/30/728387028/nba-finals-head-to-canada-as-raptors-take-on-golden-state-warriors (NPR)]
